beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output.
beats.got: Nobody can prove the agent safe, so the module is about running a check instead.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: named agent risk patterns (direct and indirect prompt injection, secrets in context, tool confusion, skill supply chain)
beats.got: A long list of jargon. No cost or payback attached to any of it.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I'm asked what I'd check first. For me that's customer data and anything touching the ledger.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent writes a request and software carries it out. Whatever is wrong with the request gets carried out too.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: It names the question I would have asked myself, before I had to raise it.

beats.trigger: the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: What may the agent read? What may it change? What must come back to a human?
beats.got: It's the same three questions I ask about any access right or approval limit, so I can follow it.

beats.trigger: Gate (human approves).
beats.got: Five kinds of fix. A human approving is the one I already know from approval limits.

beats.trigger: Accept the residual on record, or close the door.
beats.got: This reads like a risk register: write down what's left, and decide to accept it or stop.

beats.trigger: You pick it, write down what is left, and sign for it.
beats.got: If I scope it down, I'm the one who signs for what remains.

beats.trigger: Expect it to cost you a feature.
beats.got: The cheapest control is not connecting something, and that has a price too. Good that it says so. There's still no figure.

beats.trigger: You can't buy certainty.
beats.got: Safety isn't something you purchase. It's a routine the company has to keep running.

beats.trigger: a skill is a reusable check you run again instead of re-prompting from memory.
beats.got: A skill is a saved checklist I can rerun. Forty minutes for it.

beats.trigger: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The rows split into what it can verify itself and what it can't. That's useful.

beats.trigger: Push back on anything that sounds like a generic GDPR brochure.
beats.got: I tell it in a few lines what matters in my company and it shapes the check around that. I know this material.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: Twenty-two minutes of questions about lenses and risk patterns. The payoff isn't clear yet.

beats.trigger: Keep the report narrow enough to read.
beats.got: Answer briefly, hand the rest back, keep the output short enough that a person reads it.

beats.trigger: Save the authored source as a personal skill before you leave.
beats.got: Save it to my own account. Whether IT lets me do that on a company machine is a separate question.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: The agent checks are added to our existing controls and don't replace them.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: It won't promise a clean result. It promises a record of what I looked at and what I accepted.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: How to confirm the saved check is available.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: My own check finds things I missed and marks some rules "can't tell", where I would have said fine.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: Feelings again. A ranked list is useful. Calling discomfort evidence is not.

beats.trigger: Your gut is data here.
beats.got: I fix one risk and write down what remains. I'd pick by cost, not by gut.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report.
beats.got: When I can't decide, I take the report and one narrow question to legal or IT.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: One mitigation is a demo. Production means doing it for every risk. Nobody says what that costs.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: The check can be reused on the next agent. I doubt a check I built in an afternoon counts as an expert.

beats.trigger: Two things travel: the reusable check, and the root instructions file's rules for the risk you found.
beats.got: The agent writes the lessons into a file so the next session starts with them.

beats.trigger: A skill is not a deployed service and does not settle ownership.
beats.got: I can hand a colleague a skill, but nobody owns it. Who looks after it is not answered.

beats.trigger: Well-formed English is the attack surface, even via sources.
beats.got: Ordinary text in a document the agent reads can steer what it does.

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors.
beats.got: More homework before the next module.

beats.trigger: What check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two real cases, a court filing and a consultancy report for a government client, where a missing check cost someone. I'll read the Deloitte one.

take_homes: You can't prove an agent safe from what it outputs. You run a check, write down what's left, and someone signs for it.
The cheapest control is not giving the agent access, and that costs a feature.
Text in a document the agent reads can steer it, so a human approves anything that touches customers or money.

monday.move: Ask the controller to run the month-end variance commentary on last quarter's closed figures with the agent read-only, and have a person read the output before it goes anywhere. Ask IT to approve finance data for the tool, with the residual risk on one page.
monday.who: The controller, and IT for the approval
monday.stop_condition: Stop if any figure in the commentary doesn't tie to the ledger, or if IT says no.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: "You can't buy certainty" and the point that the company has to run the check itself make it harder to see this as a licence you buy. I still don't know what that work costs in people and hours.

one_line: Good on naming the residual risk and who signs for it, but it never says what the checking costs.
